title: Hungarian stitch cushion cover
subtitle: A 30 cm square cushion front worked in Hungarian stitch diamonds on 13-count canvas
excerpt: A full cushion front in Hungarian stitch on 13-count canvas. The short-long-short stitch groupings create a diamond lattice pattern across the surface. Four graduating shades of one colour fill the design. Finished size is 30 by 30 cm.
sourceNotes: Hungarian stitch layout from Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), straight canvas stitch chapter. Colour arrangement synthesised from geometric canvaswork examples in Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882).

glossaryTerms.definition: The inner stuffed form that gives a finished cushion cover its shape. Standard sizes: 30, 35, 40, and 45 cm square. The cover is usually cut 1–2 cm smaller than the pad for a firm, full result.

heroPrompt: A square cushion on a linen sofa showing a Hungarian stitch diamond pattern in four shades of sage green, natural light, white background.

content.text: This cushion front is a 156 by 156 hole square on 13-count canvas, finishing at 30 by 30 cm. Hungarian stitch groups of three stitches (over 1, over 2, over 1 thread) form diamond shapes across the canvas. Four graduating shades of sage green fill the diamonds, cycling from darkest to lightest across each column.

content.text: Palette
Shade 1: DMC 3345 / Anchor 268: dark hunter green
Shade 2: DMC 3346 / Anchor 267: hunter green
Shade 3: DMC 3347 / Anchor 266: medium yellow green
Shade 4: DMC 3348 / Anchor 264: light yellow green
Stretching the canvas
A scroll frame is essential for a cushion front of this size. A hoop would need moving repeatedly and risks marking the worked stitches.
Stitches used
Hungarian stitch: repeating groups of three upright stitches (over 1, over 2, over 1). Leave a gap of two threads between groups. The next row fills the gaps to interlock.
: repeating groups of three upright stitches (over 1, over 2, over 1), with a gap of two threads between groups in the same row to allow the next row to interlock.
Working method
Work the first horizontal row in Shade 1 across the full 156-hole width. Each group is a short stitch, a long stitch, a short stitch, then a two-thread gap before the next group.
Work the second row in Shade 2, interlocking with Row 1. The long stitch of each Row 2 group fills the gap between Row 1 groups.
Continue cycling through the four shades. The diamond lattice appears after four rows.
Fill the full 156 by 156 hole area. Block the completed canvas by dampening and pinning square to a large board overnight.
Finishing

Trim the canvas margin to 1.5 cm. Sew the backing fabric to the needlepoint front, right sides facing, along three sides. If using a zip, insert it along the bottom edge before sewing. Turn right side out, insert the
cushion pad
, and close the fourth side by hand or zip.
What to try next
The Hungarian ground stitch, a denser variant that fills the gaps with additional stitches, gives a more completely covered canvas on the same layout.
